Add puts a directory in the dream scope: sessions run in it or below it are
reviewed from the next dream on (back to the floor the first dream set,
7 days before it). A session in a git worktree of a repo in scope counts
too, with the repo's memory and commits, while the worktree exists.

--worktrees names the path prefix the repo's worktrees are made under
(say /var/tmp/app-wt-): a session whose directory starts with it belongs
to the repo even after its worktree was removed, as helpers' worktrees
usually are. Add again with another --worktrees to change it.

--root adds a tree instead: each folder directly under it is a project
in scope, as it is in the index (agent index root add), but hidden
folders, the names on the skip list (agent index skip list) and git
worktrees. A folder made under it later is in scope from the next dream
on, and one removed drops out.

Usage:
  agent dream scope add <dir> [flags]

Examples:
  agent dream scope add ~/src/app
  agent dream scope add ~/src/app --worktrees /var/tmp/app-wt-
  agent dream scope add ~/dev --root

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for add
      --root               Add a tree: each folder directly under it is a project (but hidden ones, skipped names and worktrees)
      --worktrees string   A path prefix the repo's worktrees are made under (e.g. /var/tmp/app-wt-)

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
